verdict:
tim_desk r4 (mean 5.4, lowest 5): not yet fern level. The set is now one consistent room. I projected the monitor (0.58, -0.187, turned 202 degrees), the lamp, the mug, the frame, the phone and the tray into all four cameras. Each one sits where it should wherever it is visible; in the overhead the mug is hidden under the lamp head. The window wide is the best frame of the stage, and the letters overhead is a good insert. Two things still stop the four angles cutting as one sequence.

1. The monitor plate does not yet work as the insert it is used for. It is shot from 1.40 m behind Tim's empty chair, at f/8, with no Tim. The screen fills only 32 % x 35 % of the frame, in the upper left. The brightest thing in the frame is the lit lining of the lamp shade: graded peak 218, with the bulb itself at about 200, against about 113 on the blank panel. The wall under the sill reads neutral grey (luma about 40, R-B about -1). In the window wide the same wall is warm (luma 34-36, R-B +5 to +6).

2. The lamp pool changes colour between angles. Lamp-lit pad paper has saturation 0.31 in desk and 0.26 in letters, but 0.14 in window and 0.10-0.13 in monitor. Part of this is the desk-only lamp_spot colour (1.0, 0.195, 0.013). Most of it is level. Window (lamp_spot 2.5, exposure -1.3) and monitor (2.0, -1.0) put the pool about 1.5 stops above desk (0.9, -1.5) and letters (1.0, -1.5), and AgX's highlight roll-off bleaches it.

All four frames are clean of clipping (max luma 226; 0 % of pixels at or above 250) and of text. Three problems remain:
- desk still crushes 20.6 % of its pixels below 8/255;
- the airmail chevrons put red on the desk, which the red-only-on-the-seam decision forbids;
- the parallax depth maps in out/depth/tim_desk come from earlier layouts of all three angles, and monitor has none.
answers:
Q1. Does the monitor belong to the same warm desk as the writing and window angles?
- **Props and positions: yes.** In my projection the monitor housing falls at about x 524-757 / y 217-380 in the 1920 window frame, which matches the render. It sits left of the lamp in both the window and monitor angles. The mug, photo frame, phone and tray agree wherever they are visible; in letters the mug is under the lamp head. The laptop is gone from the code.
- **Colour: it matches the window, but not the writing angle.** Lamp-lit pad paper (top 20 % of the patch, graded) measures:
  - desk: rgb 146/114/101, saturation 0.31
  - letters: rgb 140/119/103, saturation 0.26
  - window: rgb 194/177/168, saturation 0.14
  - monitor: rgb 149/136/129 on the loose sheet, saturation 0.13 (0.10 on the pad itself)

  Two causes:
  - The desk-only lamp_spot.color = (1.0, 0.195, 0.013) in apply_camera explains desk against letters (0.31 against 0.26).
  - It cannot explain window and monitor, because letters already uses st.WARM. Those two angles run the pool hot. lamp_spot trim x 2^exposure is 0.32 (desk), 0.35 (letters), 1.02 (window) and 1.0 (monitor), about 1.5 stops apart. The raw pad paper is 228/185/151 (window) and 230/192/163 (monitor), against 198/121/77 (desk) and 201/145/97 (letters), and AgX desaturates it on the way to white.

  EDL_v3 cuts desk straight to window twice (01-09 to 01-09b, 08-10 to 08-11). On those cuts the bulb looks as if it has been changed.
- **Level: the monitor plate is a little hot, and its wall has lost its warmth.**
  - Its mean luma is 41.0, against 25.0 (desk) and 27.0 (window). The blank panel inflates that figure: without the panel it is 33.4. Letters, which is mostly paper, is 60.1.
  - Compared like for like, the wall under the sill is luma about 40 with R-B about -1 in monitor (x 320-1020, y 385-490). In the window wide, right of the desk under the sill, it is 34-36 with R-B +5 to +6.
  - The relevant settings are TRIMS monitor room_fill 5.0 and exposure -1.0.
  - The brief's "big flat grey slabs" rule is about foregrounds. This is background wall, so it is a continuity problem rather than a breach of that rule.
- **Your 43.3 % figure.** I cannot reproduce it. On the graded monitor.jpg with the matte excluded (mask < 0.01), 79.3 % of pixels above luma 60 have R-B > 10. With the panel included it is 41.1 %, which may be what you measured. Either way the test is dominated by the lamp pool. What reads as not warm is the neutral wall and sill.

Q2. Which structural issue remains most visible?
- **The monitor angle has no Tim and its screen is too small.**
  - The camera stands at (0.42, 0.95, 1.40), behind his empty chair and to its left (his left).
  - In EDL_v3 this plate carries a document page (s1_p1-1.png at 03-15, 3.17 s). At 405 x 238 px of 1280 x 720, a page of text cannot be read on a phone.
  - The lamp head is smaller than the screen but much brighter (lining 218 against panel 113), so the eye goes to the lamp.
  - fern's coverage pattern (REFERENCE_DECISION) includes an over-the-shoulder at the monitor. This stage has no shot of Tim with his screen.
- **Second:** the lamp-pool jump between desk and window/monitor (Q1).
- **Third:** the desk angle is still crushed. 20.6 % of its pixels are below 8/255 and 42.4 % below 16 (luma), against the 8.6 % average that grade A was fixed to. Letters is at 13.3 % below 8/255.

Your measurements:
- **Window gap:** confirmed. On columns 620-680 the screen face (luma 23) ends at y about 352-359 and the crown begins at about 404-410. That leaves 50-55 px of dark bezel and background between them.
- **Window warmth:** confirmed. 80.0 % of pixels above luma 60 meet R-B > 10.
- **Clipping:** confirmed. Max luma is 158 (desk), 187 (letters), 218 (monitor) and 226 (window), with 0 % at or above 250.
- **Marks:** there is no text. However, the airmail chevrons (tim_desk_mats.airmail, red (0.4, 0.07, 0.06)) read as red in letters: hue about 10-17, saturation about 0.39, about 4 % of the bundle's area. They also show, smaller, in desk and window. DECISIONS says red appears only on the seam.

Plate quality:
- **Matte:** clean. Its edges go from 0 to 1 within 1-2 px, all four corners are in frame, and the raw panel is flat (luma 131, std 0.42).
- **Glass pass:** faint and warm (mean about 6/255 over the screen). Good.

Under a slow 5-10 % push:
- **Monitor:** the screen corners stay in frame (top-left 268,103 goes to about 231,77 at 10 %).
  - A round warm disc at about (745, 17-65) reaches the top edge at a 5 % push and loses its top half at 10 %: a bright practical cut by the frame.
  - It is not the night backdrop. By projection it is the lamp_spill light (a 0.04 m sphere above and behind the lamp head) mirrored in the sash glass. Its image lands at (747, 43), about 54 px across.
  - The backdrop's lit windows are rectangles, and the disc's raw colour, 241/212/187, is the lamp's warm white.
- **Window:** safe. The 50 px gap grows with the push.
  - For depth parallax, the head is about 2.3-2.5 m from the camera and the monitor about 3.1 m. A 5 cm boom shifts them about 7-9 px against each other.
  - Keep moves to pushes and horizontal drifts.
- **Desk:** the monitor housing sits just past the left edge, so a leftward drift has no rendered pixels to reveal there.
- **Letters:** the tray's top sits at y 33. A 10 % push brings it to the edge, and EDL_v3's 8.0 % (08-09) leaves about 7 px.
- **Depth maps are stale.** out/depth/tim_desk/desk.png, letters.png and window.png come from earlier layouts:
  - desk shows Tim from the other side, with the lamp on the right;
  - letters shows another arrangement;
  - window shows a farther wide, at 1280x720 for a 1920x1080 plate;
  - monitor has no map.

  tools/assemble.py only checks that a map exists, so any parallax would warp these plates with the wrong depth.

Tim's writing hand (planned Cycles close-up):
- **Grip:** at 720p the right hand reads as a clenched fist. The pen comes out low, near the ring and little fingers, with no visible thumb-and-index grip on the barrel.
- **Free hand:** the left hand lies flat, with parallel, mitten-like fingers.
- **What the beat needs:** its own close camera, a tripod grip with the nib in contact, enough subdivision on the hands to hold up at 100 mm, and an ink trace that can never read as letters.

Note: scenes/agent_loop/stages.json has no "tim_desk" entry, so I could not read the stage's brief. The module docstring is out of date for the desk camera:
- It says "from his right front", with Tim on the left of the frame and the lamp on the right. In fact loc x = +1.33 is his left side, and the frame has the lamp on the left and Tim right of centre.
- It says the camera sees the photo frame's back. At turn 121 the frame's face points about 14 degrees off the desk camera and about 49 degrees away from Tim, and the desk frame shows its face.

fixes.problem: The screen fills only 32 % of the frame width. The lamp's lit lining outshines it (218 against 113). The document page it carries in EDL_v3 (03-15) cannot be read on a phone.
fixes.fix:
Tighten CAMERAS['monitor'] (keep loc (0.42, 0.95, 1.40)) so the screen dominates. Keep the lamp head either fully in or fully out, never cut by the edge. By projection:
- Lamp out: lens 50, aim (0.71, -0.187, 1.177), which is st.MONITOR + (0.13, 0, 0). The screen spans about x 500-1155 (51 % of the width) and the lamp head falls past the right edge.
- Lamp in: lens 45, aim (0.50, -0.187, 1.177). The screen spans about 46 % of the width and the lamp head sits at about x 950-1230, which is tight.

Then:
- Check in monitor.corners.json that the screen fills 45-55 % of the width, and that all four corners stay at least 40 px inside the frame after a 10 % push.
- Fix the lamp_spill reflection first (see below). In the 50 mm framing it lands on the right edge, at about (1285, 107).
- If you also want fern's over-the-shoulder with Tim, make it a separate camera and stage it by projection (report_frame's marks) before rendering. The monitor sits about 47 degrees to his left, so from behind his left shoulder that shoulder lands at frame right. A camera between his head and the monitor (about x 0.3, y 0.8) leaves him out of frame at 45 mm.

fixes.problem: The lamp pool changes colour between angles. Lamp-lit pad paper has saturation 0.31 in desk and 0.26 in letters, but 0.14 in window and 0.10-0.13 in monitor. The desk-only lamp_spot colour explains desk against letters. The window and monitor drop comes from level: their pool runs about 1.5 stops hotter, and AgX bleaches it.

The wall under the sill reads neutral grey (luma about 40, R-B about -1). In the window wide the same wall is warm (34-36, R-B +5 to +6). The lamp shade's lit lining (peak 218) is the brightest thing in the frame.
fixes.fix:
Warm the wall and calm the lamp:
- In TRIMS['monitor'], set room_fill 5.0 to about 1.8 (the near-neutral ceiling fill is what greys this wall) and lamp_spill 3.5 to 2.0. Set lamp_spot as in the fix above, and set CAMERAS['monitor'] exposure -1.0 to -1.2.
- Warm the wall with the existing 'monitor room return'. It sits at (0.87, 0.84, 1.69), aimed at (0.61, -0.22, 0.94), just behind the monitor. Raise its trim from 1.0 and move its colour toward st.WARM.
- Light-linking 'lamp wall return' would not reach this wall: that light sits at x -1.35, aimed at the far -X wall.
- Target: the wall under the sill at luma 32-36 with R-B +4 or more, as in the window wide, and the lining's peak below the highlights of the page composited on the screen.

fixes.problem: A round warm disc at about (745, 17-65) sits 17 px under the top edge, and a 5-10 % push cuts it. It is the lamp_spill light (a 0.04 m sphere) mirrored in the sash glass, not the night backdrop: projection puts that reflection at (747, 43), about 54 px across, and its raw colour is the lamp's.
fixes.fix:
Remove the reflection at its source:
- In apply_camera, set st.LIGHTS['lamp_spill'].visible_glossy = False, for 'monitor' or for every camera. The spill is meant as a diffuse wash on the blinds and wall.
- Alternatively, exclude the sash glass objects from lamp_spill with light linking.

Do not hide the 'night' backdrop: that blacks out the view through the blinds. Do not tilt the aim down either: that lifts the disc further into the top edge. Check the new plate for any bright shape within 80 px of an edge.

After the final re-render, run `<torch python> tools/depth_estimate.py frames/raw/tim_desk/desk.png frames/raw/tim_desk/letters.png frames/raw/tim_desk/window.png frames/raw/tim_desk/monitor.png`. The tool redoes any map older than its plate. Look at each map beside its plate before cutting any parallax shot.

fixes.problem: Crushed blacks: 20.6 % of pixels are below 8/255 and 42.4 % below 16 (luma). The monitor housing sits just past the left edge, so a leftward drift reveals nothing.
fixes.fix:
Lift the shadows and give the plate room for drifts:
- The lamp_spot raise (0.9 to 1.5) lifts the lit side.
- If the frame is still above 9 % below 8/255, raise TRIMS['desk'] 'lamp wall return' from 1.5 to 2.5 and night_glow from 1.5 to 2.2. Alternatively, give CAMERAS['desk'] its own exposure of -1.3 (it now inherits the module's -1.5).
- Target under 9 % below 8/255 on the graded frame.
- If a drift is planned, render the final with 8 % overscan (sensor_width 36 x 1.08, res 1382x778), so a left drift has rendered pixels. Check that the monitor bezel either stays out of frame or enters as a whole dark shape, not a sliver.

fixes.problem: The airmail chevrons put red on the desk (hue about 10-17, saturation about 0.39 in letters, and smaller in desk and window). This breaks DECISIONS' rule that red appears only on the seam.
fixes.fix: In tim_desk_mats.airmail, change the red bar colour (0.4, 0.07, 0.06) to a muted navy-grey (0.10, 0.11, 0.16), or drop it to the white ground. Keep the blue (0.06, 0.1, 0.32) bars, so the border still reads as airmail.

fixes.problem: The writing hand reads as a fist: the pen comes out low, near the ring and little fingers, with no thumb-and-index grip. It is not ready for the Cycles writing close-up.
fixes.fix:
Pose a real grip and build the insert camera:
- In CURLS['R'], relax f_index from (20, 36, 19) to about (8, 18, 10), so it lies along the barrel. Set f_middle from (18, 28, 15) to about (22, 40, 20), so it supports the pen from below. Set THUMB_CURL['R'] from 15 to about 25, opposing the index.
- In grip_pen, set the pen at 45-50 degrees to the page, leaning back over the first knuckle, with the nib touching the sheet (tip z = TOP + PAD_H).
- Add a 'hand' camera: lens 100, about 0.35 m from the nib on the lamp side, fstop 2.0, focus on the index knuckle.
- Give the hands a level-2 subdivision for this camera.
- Animate the ink as one growing curve (bevel 0.0003, ink material) that makes a continuous wave, never letter shapes.
- Test it locally at low samples. The paid GPU render waits for the author's approval of the price (DECISIONS).

fixes.problem: From straight above, the photo frame at the top centre reads as an ambiguous dark slab with a pale edge, like a tablet on a stand. Its blank dark print behind glass reads as a dead screen. The same happens in the desk angle, where its face now points at the camera.
fixes.fix:
Give the print a pale mount: a cream border inside the wood, for example in the M['mat_board'] tone, with the print itself left dark and indistinct (no image of anyone). The face should then read as a framed photograph from above and from the desk.

Do not move the overhead aim toward +Y: 0.04 m moves the picture up about 55 px and cuts the tray, whose top sits at y 33.
